coverage: format-v3 — all five committed LiveEnvelope kinds with wrapped/unwrapped parity, replace-to-delta `_id` continuity, auth/live apply-before-ack, exact scope/expectation binding, equal-data-version authorization replacement, pending high-water, terminal delete and no-resurrection, resolution floor/shape rejection, quarantine, exact duplicate re-ACK, durable_bytes and its poll-lane analogue, connection-wide resync, tolerance negatives, negotiation/offer refusals (client_to_server), drain-cancel duplicate tolerance, arm-mismatch and grant-loss recovery, and virtual-time heartbeat/freshness/backoff

fixtures.name: durable.live_replace.basic
fixtures.notes: Whole-result refresh; the wire default. Version guard admits 41 > 40.

fixtures.name: durable.live_delta.apply_by_id
fixtures.notes: Delta-vs-replace is the server's choice (D3 fact 4): a conformant client implements both and never infers query shape from which arrives.

fixtures.name: durable.live_delta.stale_version_dropped
fixtures.notes: Version guard: a frame at or below the held version is dropped without effect (LLP 0095 §1.3).

fixtures.name: durable.replace_then_delta.identity_continuity
fixtures.notes: Format-v2 multi-step witness: live_replace establishes `_id` todo_1, then live_delta id todo_1 updates that exact row. A corpus client keyed on user field `id` cannot pass.

fixtures.name: durable.current_as_of.adopts_token_without_rows
fixtures.notes: Known CurrentAsOf obligation: advance version and adopt the mandatory fresh token without replacing or mutating held rows (LLP 0091 §0B.2).

expect.redelivery: re-acknowledge the same token without reapplying the snapshot

fixtures.name: auth.live.invalidation_snapshot_apply_then_ack
fixtures.notes: Format-v2 level-triggered sequence: quarantine first, atomically apply the superseding snapshot, only then release the exact ackToken. A redelivery remains acknowledgeable and never re-applies equal-version rows.

expect.redelivery: re-acknowledge the same token without reapplying the snapshot

fixtures.name: auth.live.invalidation_authorization_snapshot_same_data_version
fixtures.notes: Authorization and data versions are orthogonal. A first-seen exact resolution at the authenticated new authorization epoch atomically replaces rows and becomes acknowledgeable even when its snapshot data version equals the held version; the ordinary live-frame strict-greater version guard does not apply. Only an exact redelivery may skip reapplication and re-acknowledge the same token.

expect.redelivery: re-acknowledge the same token without repeating the terminal delete

fixtures.name: auth.live.invalidation_terminal_delete_apply_then_ack
fixtures.notes: A terminalDelete resolution carries no snapshot (wire omission and JSON null both decode as absent). The client first makes rows unreadable, atomically destroys the exact materialization and installs its terminal fence, and only then acknowledges the exact token. Exact redelivery re-acknowledges without repeating destruction.

fixtures.name: auth.live.invalidation_terminal_delete_blocks_ordinary_live_reuse
fixtures.notes: TERMINAL_DELETED is a one-way materialization fence. Even a numerically newer ordinary live_replace for the same subscription id is diagnosed and ignored; it cannot resurrect rows. Recreating the query requires a fresh queryInstanceId and fresh subscribe.

fixtures.name: auth.live.invalidation_newer_pending_rejects_older_resolution
fixtures.notes: Accepting revision 2 persists the exact scope/revision/witness high-water before quarantine. A later revision-1 frame with an apparently complete resolution is stale: it cannot apply rows, lower the pending floor, or acknowledge.

fixtures.name: auth.live.invalidation_owned_id_mismatched_scope_never_acknowledged
fixtures.notes: Matching subscriptionId is insufficient. The frame's full scope names queryInstanceId 2 while the held subscription owns queryInstanceId 1, so the client diagnoses and ignores it without changing or acknowledging the owned materialization.

fixtures.name: auth.live.invalidation_invalid_resolution_never_acknowledged
fixtures.notes: Step 1 accepts the valid obligation and quarantines, but its snapshot version 44 is below witness floor 45, so the resolution is diagnosed and not applied or acknowledged. Step 2 keeps that quarantine: terminalDelete plus a snapshot violates the kind/snapshot relation and the whole conflicting resolution frame is diagnosed and ignored.

rows.title: terminal delete must not carry rows

fixtures.name: auth.live.invalidation_without_snapshot_quarantines
fixtures.notes: An obligation without a satisfying snapshot makes held rows unreadable and is not acknowledged. Level-triggered delivery continues until a resolution can be applied.

fixtures.name: auth.live.foreign_obligation_never_acknowledged
fixtures.notes: The full obligation scope names a subscription this client does not hold. It is surfaced and ignored, never acknowledged on behalf of a foreign live owner.

fixtures.name: durable.resync_required.subscription_scoped
fixtures.notes: Reason strings are an open set: recovery is identical for every reason, and an unknown reason must not change the transition.

fixtures.name: durable.resync_required.connection_wide_clear_retained
fixtures.notes: No subscription_id + clear_retained: the whole outbox is untrusted (overflow class). The frame crosses the lane boundary: retained ephemeral overlays blank too (LLP 0059 cross-lane rule).

equivalenceClass.permittedEquivalent: socket close/reconnect with fresh subscribe achieving the same transitions
equivalenceClass.reference: in-place synthesized connection-wide clear-retained resync sentinel (reason durable_bytes_undecodable, client-synthesized, never wire-emitted)

fixtures.name: socket.durable_bytes.forced_resync
fixtures.notes: D3 fact 2b: a KNOWN kind with a REQUIRED recovery action. The payload's outbox lease was released at socket handoff; ignoring this frame is non-conformant (silent permanent staleness).

fixtures.name: negative.unknown_kind.skipped
fixtures.notes: Unknown kinds are skip-not-crash defense-in-depth (new kinds are always offer-gated, so a conformant server never sends one ungated). Contrast socket.durable_bytes.forced_resync: KNOWN kind, required action.

fixtures.name: negative.unknown_field.tolerated
fixtures.notes: Unknown fields on known kinds are ignored, never fatal (the acceptance grammar wins over schema closure where they diverge — LLP 0093 D1).

fixtures.name: poll.wrapped_durable.unwrap
fixtures.notes: Lane-P framing: durable envelopes arrive wrapped ({"Durable":{"payload":[u8…]}}) over the HTTP drain and unwrapped over the socket. Wrapper handling is a lane obligation, not core.

fixtures.name: poll.acknowledged_batch.malformed_item_forces_resync
fixtures.notes: The poll-lane analogue of fact 2b (LLP 0095 §1.4 T-DB-P): after the ownership cut the malformed item is lost exactly like a durable_bytes payload, so it forces the same connection-wide resync class — and must never abort the remainder. Format v2 pins sub_fixture_1 in the population and subsumes the remainder item's actions AND transitions under deliver_batch_remainder.

fixtures.name: negotiation.open.unknown_wire_version_refused
fixtures.notes: LLP 0094 §0B.3: a present unknown wireVersion refuses — a v2-needing client must never be interpreted under v1. On this refusal the client surfaces a structured capability diagnostic; silently re-opening without the offer would be exactly the undeclared degradation the refusal exists to prevent (absent-offer legacy opens are sanctioned only for clients that never needed the version).

fixtures.name: negotiation.open.unknown_auth_invalidation_protocol_refused
fixtures.notes: LLP 0094 §0C.5: both open-time offer fields follow one matrix — known binds, unknown refuses, absent degrades to legacy. Both arms enforce this (src/server.rs open_connection; cloudflare/src/coordinator.js kitOpenConnection).

fixtures.name: negotiation.socket.wire_version_required
fixtures.notes: LLP 0094 §0B.4/§0B.5 B3: the offerless-upgrade bridge is closed — kit-stream upgrades must offer the bound `snapback.v1` subprotocol. The bearer carrier is excluded before candidate matching and never counts as a version offer. The repair is offering the bound version, not retrying unchanged.

fixtures.name: negotiation.socket.unknown_wire_version_refused
fixtures.notes: LLP 0094 §0B.4: classification precedes equality — an offer set with version candidates but no known token refuses SNAPBACK_WIRE_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED, never MISMATCH, and is never silently interpreted under v1.

fixtures.name: poll.drain_cancel.redelivered_duplicates_tolerated
fixtures.notes: T-DRAIN (LLP 0095 §1.4 / LLP 0059): the drain is a leased batch with an ownership-transfer cut. A drain cancelled before the cut releases its lease and its entries redeliver, so step 2 is the exact byte-identical wrapper of step 1 arriving again. Clients MUST be duplicate-tolerant: the version guard drops the redelivered replace without effect and delivery resumes with the next version.

fixtures.name: arm.hosted_subscribe_requires_socket
fixtures.notes: T-SUB on the hosted arm (LLP 0095 §1.4; LLP 0090): subscribe refuses without a current authenticated socket session — socketless HTTP cannot arm hosted demand. The repair is establishing the managed socket first, then subscribing; retrying the socketless subscribe unchanged cannot succeed.

fixtures.name: arm.live_hosted_drain_declared_empty_blackout
fixtures.notes: T-BLACKOUT (D3 fact 2a): the hosted arm has no durable outbox — the drain is declared-empty in the capability manifest and always answers []. During a hosted socket outage the drain delivers NOTHING; a live/hosted client must not treat drain polling as a delivery or recovery lane (this is why poll/hosted is not a claimable tuple). Reconnect-resubscribe is the only recovery lane, and the empty drain is not evidence that no updates were missed.

fixtures.name: arm.socket_loss_mid_subscribe
fixtures.notes: T-LOSS + T-RECONNECT (D3 fact 2): socket loss drops the connection's durable subscriptions server-side, including one whose subscribe was still in flight — the ambiguous in-flight outcome resolves to DROPPED and is never assumed established. Recovery is bounded-backoff reconnect then fresh subscribe: with `supersedes` (and the mandatory superseded/supersessionRefusal response witness) for the established id, and a plain fresh subscribe for the never-established one.

fixtures.name: grant.connection_token_invalid_reopens_everything
fixtures.notes: T-GRANT-LOSS (LLP 0095 §1.4/§4.4): SNAPBACK_CONNECTION_TOKEN_INVALID covers both the local idle reap and hosted grant expiry — the client cannot distinguish them at the refusal, and the recovery is identical: re-open the connection (a fresh grant is a fresh connection identity) and re-establish EVERY subscription, treating retained overlays as void. Grant-refresh-only recovery would resurrect the fake-healthy-handle defect class.

fixtures.name: poll.wrapped_live_delta.unwrap
fixtures.notes: Wrapped/unwrapped parity: the exact live_delta envelope of durable.live_delta.apply_by_id in Lane-P framing. Unwrapping is a lane obligation; the inner judgment is identical to the core fixture.

fixtures.name: poll.wrapped_resync_required.subscription_scoped
fixtures.notes: Wrapped/unwrapped parity for durable.resync_required.subscription_scoped: reason strings stay an open set and the transition is reason-independent in either framing.

fixtures.name: poll.wrapped_resync_required.connection_wide_clear_retained
fixtures.notes: Wrapped/unwrapped parity for durable.resync_required.connection_wide_clear_retained: the cross-lane clear-retained rule (LLP 0059) is framing-independent — retained ephemeral overlays blank in Lane-P framing too.

fixtures.name: poll.wrapped_current_as_of.adopts_token_without_rows
fixtures.notes: Wrapped/unwrapped parity for durable.current_as_of.adopts_token_without_rows: adopt the mandatory fresh token and advance the version without touching held rows, in Lane-P framing.

fixtures.name: timing.heartbeat.ping_and_pong_freshness
fixtures.notes: T-HB (LLP 0095 §1.4; LLP 0034 D0/D1): 5 s heartbeat ping, 15 s freshness budget. The advance to t=5000 obligates a liveness probe; the pong refreshes the freshness budget, so the further advance to t=14999 obligates more pings (send_ping repeats within an interval under the rule-4 set judgment) but never the loss path — the budget from the last server activity is not exhausted.

fixtures.name: timing.freshness.budget_exhausted_forces_loss
fixtures.notes: T-HB's loss half (LLP 0095 §1.4; LLP 0034 D0/D1): no server activity for the whole 15 s freshness budget while the socket still claims open forces the loss path — the client declares the socket lost (force_socket_loss) rather than trusting a silent TCP session, and every durable subscription drops per T-LOSS. Pings during the interval repeat under the rule-4 set judgment.

fixtures.name: timing.reconnect.backoff_bounds
fixtures.notes: T-LOSS backoff (LLP 0095 §1.4; LLP 0034 D0/D1): bounded backoff 250 ms → 10 s. No reconnect attempt may fire before 250 ms after the loss; thereafter attempts repeat with growing delays capped at 10 s, so over the second interval consecutive attempts are never more than pacing.maxIntervalMs apart. Each successful attempt is T-RECONNECT's fresh subscribe with supersedes — not judged here, since a fixture carries no live server.
